state:
Goal `tools-php-differences`: 7 of the chapter's 12 features are done. This session added `functions-constants-and-scope` and `types-and-conversions`. `bun nv proofs --owed --group tools:php-differences` lists the 5 still owed: `operators`, `control-flow`, `what-parses-but-behaves-differently`, `the-tools-you-do-not-install` and `two-spellings-side-by-side`.
So far the proofs have corrected eleven rows of `docs/reference/tools/30-php-differences.md`. This session fixed four in § *Types and conversions*. `fn($x) => …` is `E0808`, not `E0101`, and may leave the type out under a `callable(int): int` type. An `array<T>` is not an `Iterable<T>`. `never` compiles and runs. `public ?int $x = null;` compiles, and `E0472` is an expression default such as `1 + 2`.
A `never` method whose body reaches its end compiles, and the call returns to the caller. Gap `nvs-types/a-never-method-that-reaches-its-end-returns` records it and names the rule sentence the fix rewrites.
Gap `nvs-syntax/a-second-namespace-statement-in-one-file-compiles` is still open, and `nvs-runtime/a-loop-that-only-concatenates-never-stops` still marks the arrays-and-strings attack.
Each feature here owes one example, one attack and one case carrying `// covers:`. It owes no `about.md` or bench. `the-tools-you-do-not-install` also owes help: its section shows no code block.
Narrowing happens on the true edge alone (`rule:types/narrowing`): `if ($q is null) { return; }` leaves `$q` at `?int` after it, so an example tests `is int` instead.
